records.source: וַיְהִי֙ כְּכַלּ֣וֹת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לִבְנ֥וֹת אֶת־בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־חֵ֣שֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָפֵ֖ץ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ
records.gloss: And it was, when finished Solomon building the house of Yahweh and the house of the king and all [the] desire of Solomon which he delighted to do,
pieces: After Solomon had completed the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the royal palace, and everything else he had set his heart on making,

L.1: And it happened, when Solomon had finished building the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the house of the king, and all the desire of Solomon that he had been pleased to do,

R.1: Solomon finished building {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and the royal palace. He also finished everything else he had wanted to build.

decisions.choice: when Solomon had finished: a time clause that leads into verse 2
decisions.reason: The verse sets the time for what follows; the main statement, that the LORD appeared to Solomon, comes in verse 2. Verse 10 puts the end of the building work twenty years after it began (6:38; 7:1).

decisions.choice: the desire of Solomon that he was pleased to do: every building project he longed to carry out
decisions.reason: The noun means something longed for or set one's heart on. Here it sums up the rest of Solomon's building, which verse 19 describes with the same word.

decisions.choice: the house of the king: Solomon's royal palace
decisions.reason: This is the palace complex described in 7:1-12, which took thirteen years to build.

decisions.choice: the royal palace (Balanced, Readable); the LORD's temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: "House" means a temple when it is God's and a palace when it is the king's. Balanced keeps "house" for God's house, as in chapter 3; Readable says "temple" there, and both say "royal palace" for the king's. Readable makes the verse a sentence of its own.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} appears to Solomon again

records.source: וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה שֵׁנִ֑ית כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלָ֖יו בְּגִבְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: and appeared Yahweh to Solomon a second [time], as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Solomon a second time, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had appeared to him at Gibeon.

L.2: that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Solomon a second time, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had appeared to him at Gibeon.

R.2: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Solomon again, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had appeared to him at Gibeon.

decisions.choice: a second time, as at Gibeon: a second meeting like the dream of 3:4-15
decisions.reason: The first time, at the start of his reign, the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and offered him whatever he asked (3:5). The second appearance comes when his building is complete and answers his prayer at the dedication of the house (8:22-53).

decisions.choice: the second appearance follows the end of all the building
decisions.reason: Verse 1 ties this appearance to the completion of all Solomon's work, not only the temple. The text does not say how long after the dedication of chapter 8 it came.

decisions.choice: that
decisions.reason: Literal joins the verse to the "when" clause of verse 1 with "that", as the Hebrew "and it happened, when ... and" does.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו שָׁ֠מַעְתִּי אֶת־תְּפִלָּתְךָ֣ וְאֶת־תְּחִנָּתְךָ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְחַנַּ֣נְתָּה לְפָנַי֒ הִקְדַּ֗שְׁתִּי אֶת־הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנִ֔תָה לָשֽׂוּם־שְׁמִ֥י שָׁ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם וְהָי֨וּ עֵינַ֧י וְלִבִּ֛י שָׁ֖ם כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to him, I have heard your prayer and your supplication which you have sought favor before me; I have consecrated the house this which you have built to put my name there until forever, and will be my eyes and my heart there all the days.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "I have heard your prayer and the plea for mercy you made to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I have set apart as holy this house you have built, and I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name there forever. My eyes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart will always be there.

L.3: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "I have heard your prayer and your plea for favor that you made before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I have consecrated this house that you have built, to put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name there forever; and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart will be there all the days.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "I have heard your prayer. I have heard you ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for mercy. I have made this temple you built a holy place. I have chosen it to carry {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name forever. I will always watch over it and care for it.

decisions.choice: I have heard your prayer: the answer to Solomon's prayer at the dedication
decisions.reason: Solomon had asked the LORD to hear the prayers made at this house and to keep his eyes open toward it night and day (8:28-30, 52). This is the reply, and the warning that follows in verses 6-9 echoes the disasters his prayer had named (8:33-34, 46-50).

decisions.choice: to put my name there: to claim the house as his own and make it the place where he is known and called on
decisions.reason: The "name" stands for the LORD himself as he makes himself known. Deuteronomy speaks of the place the LORD would choose "to put his name there" (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11), and Solomon used the same language (8:16, 29). The LORD's presence is not confined there (8:27), but this is where his name is honored.

decisions.choice: my eyes and my heart will be there: the LORD's constant attention and care
decisions.reason: Eyes stand for watching over something, and the heart for one's concern and will. "All the days" means always, without a break.

decisions.choice: consecrated: made holy, set apart for the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something holy, that is, set apart as belonging to God. The LORD himself now does what the dedication ceremony had asked for.

decisions.choice: I have chosen it to carry my name ... I will always watch over it and care for it
decisions.reason: Readable explains both pictures instead of reproducing them: putting the name becomes choosing the house to carry his name, and eyes and heart become watching over and caring for it.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֞ה אִם־תֵּלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנַ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר הָלַ֜ךְ דָּוִ֤ד אָבִ֨יךָ֙ בְּתָם־לֵבָ֣ב וּבְיֹ֔שֶׁר לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֑יךָ חֻקַּ֥י וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י תִּשְׁמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And you, if you will walk before me as walked David your father in integrity of heart and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded you; my statutes and my judgments you will keep,
pieces: As for you, if you live before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as your father David did, with a whole heart and with uprightness, doing everything I have commanded you and keeping {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings,

L.4: And you, if you walk before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded you, [and] keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments,

R.4: Now you must live faithfully before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as your father David did. Your heart must be sincere and honest. Do everything I have commanded you, and obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and rules.

decisions.choice: walk before me: live one's whole life in the LORD's sight and service
decisions.reason: The same picture is used of Abraham (Genesis 17:1) and of David (3:6), and in David's charge to Solomon (2:4).

decisions.choice: integrity of heart and uprightness: an undivided and honest heart
decisions.reason: The first noun means completeness or wholeness: a heart not split between the LORD and anything else. The second means straightness, doing what is right. Solomon's heart later fails exactly here (11:4).

decisions.choice: if ...: the condition on which the promise of verse 5 depends
decisions.reason: The verse is the first half of a conditional sentence; verse 5 gives the result. The LORD's promise to Solomon's line depends on his obedience, as 2:4 and 8:25 had already said.

decisions.choice: statutes and rulings (Balanced); laws and rules (Readable)
decisions.reason: These follow the book-wide wording for this pair of terms.

decisions.choice: you must ... (verse 5: If you do)
decisions.reason: Readable states the conditions as plain sentences and gives the "if" at the start of verse 5, as it does in 2:4. The meaning is the same: the promise depends on these conditions.

records.source: וַהֲקִ֨מֹתִ֜י אֶת־כִּסֵּ֧א מַֽמְלַכְתְּךָ֛ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעֹלָ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי עַל־דָּוִ֤ד אָבִ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I spoke concerning David your father, saying, Not will be cut off for you a man from on [the] throne of Israel.
pieces: then I will make the throne of your kingdom over Israel secure forever, as I promised your father David when I said, 'There will always be a man of your line on the throne of Israel.'

L.5: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I spoke concerning David your father, saying, 'A man will not be cut off for you from on the throne of Israel.'

R.5: If you do, I will make sure that your family rules over Israel forever. That is what I promised your father David. I told him, 'One of your family will always sit on Israel's throne.'

decisions.choice: as I spoke concerning David your father: the promise of 2 Samuel 7
decisions.reason: The LORD promised David through Nathan that his throne would stand forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). David passed it on to Solomon with its condition (2:4), and Solomon recalled it in his prayer (8:25).

decisions.choice: a man will not be cut off for you from the throne: you will never lack a descendant on the throne
decisions.reason: "Cut off" means removed or brought to an end. The promise is that David's line will never be without a king of his own family on Israel's throne.

decisions.choice: wording of 2:4 reused
decisions.reason: The promise is the same as in 2:4, so each level repeats the wording it uses there.

records.source: אִם־שׁ֨וֹב תְּשֻׁב֜וּן אַתֶּ֤ם וּבְנֵיכֶם֙ מֵֽאַחֲרַ֔י וְלֹ֤א תִשְׁמְרוּ֙ מִצְוֺתַ֣י חֻקֹּתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֗ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: If turning you turn back, you and your sons, from after me, and not you keep my commandments, my statutes, which I have set before you, and you go and serve gods other and bow down to them,
pieces: But if you or your descendants turn away from following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and do not keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes that I have set before you, and instead go off to serve other gods and bow down to them,

L.6: [But] if you indeed turn back, you or your {{gender:children|sons}}, from [following] after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and do not keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, that I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

R.6: But suppose you or your descendants turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Suppose you do not obey the commands and laws I have given you, but you go and serve other gods and worship them.

decisions.choice: you or your sons: the address widens from Solomon to his line and the people
decisions.reason: From here to verse 9 every "you" is plural, while verses 3-5 spoke to Solomon alone. The warning now covers Solomon, the kings after him and, as verse 7 shows, all Israel.

decisions.choice: if you indeed turn back: an emphatic form
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled, a way of stressing it: if you do turn away. It makes the warning firm, not tentative.

decisions.choice: serve other gods and bow down to them: breaking the first demand of the covenant
decisions.reason: Worshiping other gods breaks the first two commandments (Exodus 20:3-5) and is the sin that Deuteronomy says would bring exile (Deuteronomy 29:25-27).

decisions.choice: your children (Literal, with "sons" as the setting); your descendants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means the generations after Solomon, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants".

decisions.choice: But suppose ...
decisions.reason: Readable states the conditions as their own sentences and gives the result in verse 7 with "then".

records.source: וְהִכְרַתִּ֣י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵעַ֨ל פְּנֵ֤י הָאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־הַבַּ֨יִת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְדַּ֣שְׁתִּי לִשְׁמִ֔י אֲשַׁלַּ֖ח מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑י וְהָיָ֧ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לְמָשָׁ֥ל וְלִשְׁנִינָ֖ה בְּכָל־הָעַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: then I will cut off Israel from on [the] face of the ground which I have given to them, and the house which I have consecrated for my name I will send away from on my face; and will be Israel for a proverb and for a taunt among all the peoples.
pieces: then I will cut Israel off from the land I have given them, and I will cast this house that I have made holy for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight. Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.

L.7: then I will cut off Israel from the face of the land that I have given them; and the house that I have consecrated for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name I will send away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence; and Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.

R.7: Then I will remove Israel from the land I gave them. I will reject this temple that I made holy for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face away from it. People of every nation will tell of what happened to Israel as a warning, and they will make fun of it.

decisions.choice: cut off Israel from the face of the land: remove the people from their land
decisions.reason: The threat is exile, as the covenant curses warned (Deuteronomy 28:63-64). The book ends with it happening to Israel (2 Kings 17:23) and to Judah (2 Kings 25:21).

decisions.choice: send away from my presence: reject and cast off
decisions.reason: The verb is used of sending someone away for good. The house the LORD has just made holy will be cast out of his sight, as Jeremiah later warned (Jeremiah 7:14-15).

decisions.choice: a proverb and a byword: a saying about Israel's fate and a sharp taunt
decisions.reason: The first word is a saying people quote, here an example of disaster; the second is a cutting word of mockery. The same pair appears in the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 28:37).

decisions.choice: I will turn my face away from it; tell of what happened to Israel as a warning, and make fun of it
decisions.reason: Readable explains "send away from my face" and the two nouns, which have no simple plain-English equivalents.

records.source: וְהַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה עֶלְי֔וֹן כָּל־עֹבֵ֥ר עָלָ֖יו יִשֹּׁ֣ם וְשָׁרָ֑ק וְאָמְר֗וּ עַל־מֶ֨ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ כָּ֔כָה לָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את וְלַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And the house this will be high; every [one] passing by it will be appalled and will hiss, and they will say, For what did Yahweh do thus to the land this and to the house this?
pieces: And this house, high as it stands, will leave everyone who passes by it appalled. They will hiss and ask, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dealt like this with this land and this house?'

L.8: And [as for] this house, [which] will be high, everyone passing by it will be appalled and will hiss; and they will say, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} done thus to this land and to this house?'

R.8: This temple stands high and grand now, but everyone who passes by it will be shocked. They will hiss in horror and ask, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} done this to the land and to this temple?'

decisions.choice: will be high: read as "though it is now lofty"
alternatives: will become a heap of ruins
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says this house "will be high" (or "most high"), which is hard to fit with the ruin the verse describes. Taken as it stands, it means: lofty as this house is, everyone will be appalled at it. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 7:21 reads "which was exalted". Some early translations read "will become a heap of ruins", which may reflect a different Hebrew word (compare Micah 3:12).

decisions.choice: appalled and will hiss: shock and scorn at a ruin
decisions.reason: Hissing or whistling was a gesture of horror and mockery at a place struck by disaster (Jeremiah 19:8; 49:17; Lamentations 2:15-16).

decisions.choice: why has the LORD done thus to this land: the question of Deuteronomy 29
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy foresees the nations asking the same question about the ruined land and gives the same answer (Deuteronomy 29:23-25; compare Jeremiah 22:8-9).

decisions.choice: high as it stands (Balanced); stands high and grand now, but (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the contrast explicit, since "this house will be high" alone would sound like a promise.

decisions.choice: hiss
decisions.reason: "Hiss" keeps the sound of the gesture; Readable adds "in horror" so it is not taken as anger.

records.source: וְאָמְר֗וּ עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָזְב֜וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצִ֣יא אֶת־אֲבֹתָם֮ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ וַֽיַּחֲזִ֨קוּ֙ בֵּאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲו֥וּלָהֶ֖ם וַיַּעַבְדֻ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֗ן הֵבִ֤יא יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃פ
records.gloss: And they will say, Because that they forsook Yahweh their God who brought out their fathers from [the] land of Egypt, and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them; therefore has brought Yahweh on them all the disaster this.
pieces: And people will answer, 'Because they abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who brought their ancestors out of the land of Egypt, and they embraced other gods and worshiped and served them. That is why {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought all this disaster on them.'"

L.9: And they will say, 'Because they forsook {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them; therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought on them all this disaster.'"

R.9: And people will answer, 'It is because they left {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who brought their ancestors out of Egypt. They held on to other gods and worshiped and served them. That is why {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought all this trouble on them.'"

decisions.choice: they will say ... they forsook: the onlookers answer, and "they" are the people of Israel
decisions.reason: The same passers-by of verse 8 give the answer, and the people they speak of are Israel, who were brought out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: took hold of: clung to, attached themselves firmly to
decisions.reason: The verb means to grasp and hold on tight. Israel let go of the LORD and held fast to other gods instead.

decisions.choice: disaster: calamity, harm that comes on them
decisions.reason: The word is often translated "evil", but here it means the trouble and ruin that the LORD brings as judgment, not moral wrong.

decisions.choice: ancestors; people will answer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", and name the speakers as "people", since "they" would be unclear. The closing double quote ends the LORD's speech that began in verse 3.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י מִקְצֵה֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־בָּנָ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת־שְׁנֵ֣י הַבָּתִּ֑ים אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] end of twenty years which built Solomon the two houses, the house of Yahweh and the house of the king,
pieces: At the end of the twenty years it took Solomon to build the two houses, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house and the royal palace,

L.10: And it happened at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses, the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the house of the king,

R.10: It took Solomon twenty years to build the two buildings, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and the royal palace.

decisions.choice: twenty years: seven for the temple and thirteen for the palace
decisions.reason: The temple took seven years (6:38) and the palace thirteen (7:1), so the whole building program lasted twenty years.

decisions.choice: a time clause that runs on into verse 11
decisions.reason: The sentence begins here and reaches its main statement in verse 11, "then King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities"; the first half of verse 11 is an aside about Hiram.

decisions.choice: It took Solomon twenty years ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the time clause a sentence of its own, and gives the main statement in verse 11 with "So".

records.heading: Solomon's other works

records.source: חִירָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ־צֹ֠ר נִשָּׂ֨א אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה בַּעֲצֵי֩ אֲרָזִ֨ים וּבַעֲצֵ֧י בְרוֹשִׁ֛ים וּבַזָּהָ֖ב לְכָל־חֶפְצ֑וֹ אָ֡ז יִתֵּן֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה לְחִירָם֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים עִ֔יר בְּאֶ֖רֶץ הַגָּלִֽיל׃
records.gloss: Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with timber of cedars and with timber of cypresses and with gold according to all his desire, then gave the king Solomon to Hiram twenty cities in [the] land of the Galilee.
pieces: since Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber and gold he wanted, King Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in the region of Galilee.

L.11: Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with cedar timber and with cypress timber and with gold, as much as he desired; then King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.

R.11: Hiram, the king of Tyre, had given Solomon all the cedar and cypress wood and gold he wanted. So King Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in the area of Galilee.

decisions.choice: Hiram had supplied Solomon: the agreement of chapter 5
decisions.reason: Hiram sent cedar and cypress from Lebanon in return for wheat and oil (5:22-25), and the two kings made a treaty (5:26). The gold is not mentioned there; it may be the gold of verse 14.

decisions.choice: cypress: a tall conifer of Lebanon
decisions.reason: The tree is not identified with certainty; it may be a cypress, a juniper or a fir. It is named beside cedar as fine building timber (5:22; 6:15, 34).

decisions.choice: twenty cities in the land of Galilee: towns in the north, on the border of Tyre's territory
decisions.reason: Galilee here is the district of northern Israel next to Phoenicia, in the area given to Asher (Joshua 19:24-31). "Cities" can name small walled towns or villages.

decisions.choice: then ... gave: the payment came when the building was done
decisions.reason: "Then" ties the gift to the end of the twenty years in verse 10. Whether the towns were a payment for Hiram's supplies or a pledge for them is not said.

decisions.choice: towns; region (Balanced), area (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Towns" suits places of this size better than "cities", and "region" or "area" shows that "the land of Galilee" is a district, not a country. Balanced begins with "since" to carry on the sentence from verse 10.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֤א חִירָם֙ מִצֹּ֔ר לִרְאוֹת֙ אֶת־הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַן־ל֖וֹ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְלֹ֥א יָשְׁר֖וּ בְּעֵינָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And came out Hiram from Tyre to see the cities which had given to him Solomon, and not they were right in his eyes.
pieces: But when Hiram came from Tyre to see the towns Solomon had given him, they did not please him.

L.12: And Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, and they were not right in his eyes.

R.12: Hiram went from Tyre to look at the towns Solomon had given him. But he did not like them.

decisions.choice: they were not right in his eyes: they did not please him
decisions.reason: "Right in someone's eyes" means acceptable or pleasing to that person. Hiram thought the towns a poor return.

decisions.choice: did not please him (Balanced); did not like them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom in plain words.

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֚ה הֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תָּה לִּ֖י אָחִ֑י וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כָּב֔וּל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And he said, What [are] the cities these which you have given to me, my brother? And he called them land of Cabul until the day this.
pieces: He said, "What kind of towns are these you have given me, my brother?" So they have been called the land of Cabul to this day.

L.13: And he said, "What [are] these cities that you have given me, my brother?" And he called them the land of Cabul, to this day.

R.13: He said, "My brother, what kind of towns are these that you have given me?" So that area was called the land of Cabul, which sounds like "good for nothing". It is still called that to this day.

decisions.choice: what are these cities: a scornful question
decisions.reason: Hiram is not asking for information; he is expressing his low opinion of the gift.

decisions.choice: my brother: the address of an ally of equal rank
decisions.reason: Kings bound by a treaty called each other "brother" (compare 20:32-33). Solomon and Hiram had made such a treaty (5:26), so the word is polite even while Hiram complains.

decisions.choice: Cabul: a name that sounds like "as nothing"
decisions.reason: The name was understood as a play on words: in Hebrew it sounds like "like nothing" or "as good as nothing", which fits Hiram's complaint. The exact sense of the wordplay is not certain. There was a town Cabul in the territory of Asher (Joshua 19:27), so the name may be older than the story and taken up as a joke.

decisions.choice: he called them ... to this day: the name was still used in the writer's own day
decisions.reason: "He called" may mean Hiram or may be impersonal, "they were called". "To this day" means the time of the writer, as at 8:8.

decisions.choice: they have been called (Balanced); that area was called (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave open who gave the name, as the impersonal sense allows.

decisions.choice: which sounds like "good for nothing"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay so the reader can see why the name stuck. The exact sense of the pun is uncertain, but its point, that the towns were worth little, is clear from Hiram's words.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח חִירָ֖ם לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים כִּכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And had sent Hiram to the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold.
pieces: Hiram had sent the king {{units:about 9,000 pounds|120 talents}} of gold.

L.14: And Hiram had sent to the king 120 talents of gold.

R.14: Hiram had sent King Solomon {{units:about 9,000 pounds|120 talents}} of gold.

decisions.choice: had sent: the gold Hiram had already supplied
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as "had sent", looking back to the gold of verse 11, or as "then sent", a payment for the towns despite his complaint. The first fits the flow from verse 11 better.

decisions.choice: talent: the largest weight, about 75 pounds
decisions.reason: A talent was 3,000 shekels. 120 talents of gold is about 9,000 pounds, or about 4 1/2 tons.

decisions.choice: about 9,000 pounds (with 120 talents as the setting)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern weight, with the talent as the alternative, as for every measure.

records.source: וְזֶ֨ה דְבַר־הַמַּ֜ס אֲשֶֽׁר־הֶעֱלָ֣ה׀הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנוֹת֩ אֶת־בֵּ֨ית יְהוָ֤ה וְאֶת־בֵּיתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־הַמִּלּ֔וֹא וְאֵ֖ת חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֶת־חָצֹ֥ר וְאֶת־מְגִדּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־גָּֽזֶר׃
records.gloss: And this [is] the account of the forced labor which raised the king Solomon to build the house of Yahweh and his house and the Millo and [the] wall of Jerusalem and Hazor and Megiddo and Gezer.
pieces: This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon conscripted to build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, his own palace, the Millo, Jerusalem's wall, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer.

L.15: And this [is] the account of the forced labor that King Solomon raised to build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and his own house and the Millo and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor and Megiddo and Gezer.

R.15: This is the record of the workers King Solomon forced to work for him. He used them to build {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, his own palace, the Millo (a supporting terrace), and the wall around Jerusalem. He also had them build up the towns of Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer.

decisions.choice: this is the account of: a heading for the list that follows
decisions.reason: The word can mean "word", "matter" or "account". It introduces verses 15-23, on who did Solomon's building work and what they built.

decisions.choice: forced labor: workers called up by the king to work without pay
decisions.reason: Kings conscripted men for their building works (4:6; 5:27-28). This verse names the projects; verses 20-22 say who was made to do the work.

decisions.choice: the Millo: probably a terrace of filled-in earth and stone in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: See 2 Samuel 5:9. The name comes from the verb "to fill". Verse 24 says when Solomon built it.

decisions.choice: Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer: fortress cities on the main roads
decisions.reason: Hazor guarded the north, Megiddo the pass into the Valley of Jezreel, and Gezer the road from the coast up to Jerusalem. Fortifying them secured the routes through Solomon's kingdom.

decisions.choice: the Millo (a supporting terrace)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the Millo briefly, as in 2 Samuel 5:9.

decisions.choice: conscripted (Balanced); forced to work (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is "raised" or "brought up", used of calling up a workforce; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

records.source: פַּרְעֹ֨ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֜יִם עָלָ֗ה וַיִּלְכֹּ֤ד אֶת־גֶּ֨זֶר֙ וַיִּשְׂרְפָ֣הּ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְאֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב בָּעִ֖יר הָרָ֑ג וַֽיִּתְּנָהּ֙ שִׁלֻּחִ֔ים לְבִתּ֖וֹ אֵ֥שֶׁת שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃
records.gloss: Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, and the Canaanite[s] living in the city he had killed, and he had given it [as] a dowry to his daughter, [the] wife of Solomon.
pieces: Pharaoh king of Egypt had come up and captured Gezer. He burned it down, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.

L.16: Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, and he had killed the Canaanites living in the city, and had given it [as] a dowry to his daughter, the wife of Solomon.

R.16: Before this, Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had attacked and captured Gezer. He burned the city and killed the Canaanites who lived there. Then he gave it to his daughter as a wedding gift when she married Solomon.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh had gone up: an aside explaining how Gezer came to Solomon
decisions.reason: The verse looks back to an earlier event to explain why Gezer, named in verse 15, was Solomon's to rebuild. Pharaoh is not named.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites living in the city: Gezer had stayed Canaanite
decisions.reason: Israel had never driven the Canaanites out of Gezer (Joshua 16:10; Judges 1:29). Pharaoh's attack ended their hold on the city.

decisions.choice: dowry: a parting gift from a father to his daughter at her marriage
decisions.reason: The word means something "sent off" with a person. Here it is the gift Pharaoh gave when his daughter left home to marry Solomon (3:1; compare Micah 1:14).

decisions.choice: as a wedding gift when she married Solomon
decisions.reason: Readable says "wedding gift" and spells out the occasion, which "his daughter, Solomon's wife" implies.

records.source: וַיִּ֤בֶן שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֶת־גָּ֔זֶר וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית חֹרֹ֖ן תַּחְתּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And built Solomon Gezer and Beth Horon lower,
pieces: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, and Lower Beth-horon,

L.17: And Solomon built Gezer and Lower Beth-horon,

R.17: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer and built up the town of Lower Beth-horon.

decisions.choice: built: rebuilt and fortified
decisions.reason: "Build" is used for rebuilding a ruined town and for strengthening one. Gezer had been burned (verse 16), so here it means rebuilt.

decisions.choice: Lower Beth-horon: a town guarding the pass up from the coastal plain
decisions.reason: Upper and Lower Beth-horon stood on the main road from the coast to the hill country north of Jerusalem (Joshua 10:10-11; 16:3).

decisions.choice: the list runs on to verse 19
decisions.reason: The list of building works continues through verses 18-19, all governed by "Solomon built".

decisions.choice: rebuilt Gezer; built up Lower Beth-horon (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "rebuilt" for Gezer, and Readable makes the verse a full sentence.

records.source: וְאֶֽת־בַּעֲלָ֛ת וְאֶת־תַּדְמֹ֥ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: and Baalath and Tamar in the wilderness in the land,
pieces: Baalath, and Tamar in the wilderness, within the land,

L.18: and Baalath and Tamar in the wilderness, in the land,

R.18: He also built Baalath, and Tamar in the desert part of the land.

decisions.choice: Tamar: the name as written; it is read aloud as Tadmor
decisions.reason: The consonants of the Hebrew text spell Tamar, a place on the southern edge of the land (Ezekiel 47:19; 48:28), which fits "in the wilderness, in the land". The traditional reading and the parallel in 2 Chronicles 8:4 have Tadmor, the desert oasis far to the northeast, later called Palmyra.

decisions.choice: in the land: inside Solomon's own territory
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and seems to need something after it, such as "of Judah". As it stands it says that this wilderness town lay within the land.

decisions.choice: Baalath: a town in the territory of Dan
decisions.reason: Baalath is listed among Dan's towns (Joshua 19:44), not far from Gezer and Beth-horon.

decisions.choice: in the desert part of the land
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two phrases into one plain description.

records.source: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־עָרֵ֤י הַֽמִּסְכְּנוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֣וּ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וְאֵת֙ עָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְאֵ֖ת עָרֵ֣י הַפָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת׀חֵ֣שֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָשַׁק֙ לִבְנ֤וֹת בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וּבַלְּבָנ֔וֹן וּבְכֹ֖ל אֶ֥רֶץ מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and all the cities of the stores which belonged to Solomon, and the cities of the chariotry and the cities of the horsemen, and the desire of Solomon which he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all [the] land of his dominion.
pieces: and all the store cities that Solomon had, the towns for his chariots and for his horsemen, and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout all the land he ruled.

L.19: and all the cities of storage that belonged to Solomon, and the cities of the chariots and the cities of the horsemen, and the desire of Solomon that he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion.

R.19: He built all the towns where he stored supplies, and the towns for his chariots and his horsemen. He built whatever he wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and everywhere in the land he ruled.

decisions.choice: cities of storage: towns where grain and supplies were stored
decisions.reason: Royal store cities held food and supplies for the army and the court, like those Israel built for Pharaoh (Exodus 1:11).

decisions.choice: horsemen: the men who rode or drove the horses, or the horses themselves
decisions.reason: The word can mean either. Solomon's chariots and horses are counted in 5:6 and 10:26.

decisions.choice: the desire of Solomon that he desired: whatever he set his heart on
decisions.reason: The noun and verb repeat the word of verse 1: these were the projects Solomon wanted for himself.

decisions.choice: Lebanon: the mountains to the north where the timber came from
decisions.reason: Solomon had work done in Lebanon itself (5:20-23); the text does not say what he built there.

decisions.choice: whatever Solomon desired to build; the land he ruled
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "the desire ... that he desired" into a plain clause, and "the land of his dominion" into "the land he ruled".

records.source: כָּל־הָ֠עָם הַנּוֹתָ֨ר מִן־הָאֱמֹרִ֜י הַחִתִּ֤י הַפְּרִזִּי֙ הַחִוִּ֣י וְהַיְבוּסִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־מִבְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: All the people who remained of the Amorite[s], the Hittite[s], the Perizzite[s], the Hivite[s] and the Jebusite[s], who not [were] of [the] sons of Israel they,
pieces: As for all the people who were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, who were not {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}},

L.20: All the people who were left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who [were] not of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel,

R.20: Some of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites were still left in the land. These people were not {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites: the peoples of Canaan before Israel
decisions.reason: These names belong to the standard list of the land's earlier inhabitants (Exodus 3:8; Deuteronomy 7:1; Joshua 9:1). The Canaanites, usually in the list, have already appeared in verse 16.

decisions.choice: all the people who were left: placed first and taken up again in verse 21
decisions.reason: The verse names the group, and verse 21 continues "their descendants ... Solomon raised them". The sentence ends there.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable states who these peoples were in sentences of their own before verse 21 says what Solomon did with them.

records.source: בְּנֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נֹתְר֤וּ אַחֲרֵיהֶם֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יָכְל֛וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַֽחֲרִימָ֑ם וַיַּעֲלֵ֤ם שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְמַס־עֹבֵ֔ד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: their sons who remained after them in the land whom not were able [the] sons of Israel to devote them to destruction, and raised them Solomon for forced labor of slaving until the day this.
pieces: their descendants who were still left in the land, whom the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had not been able to devote to destruction, Solomon conscripted as forced labor, as slaves, to this day.

L.21: their {{gender:children|sons}} who were left after them in the land, whom the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel had not been able to devote to destruction, Solomon raised them for forced labor as slaves, to this day.

R.21: They were the descendants of the peoples the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had not been able to destroy completely. Solomon forced them to work as slaves, and they still do so to this day.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction: destroy completely as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the ban on the nations of Canaan (Deuteronomy 7:2; 20:17). Israel had not carried it out, and the survivors were made to work instead, as Judges 1:28-35 records.

decisions.choice: forced labor as slaves: lasting, compulsory service
decisions.reason: The phrase adds "slaving" to the usual word for forced labor. These peoples were held in permanent servitude to the crown, unlike the Israelites of verse 22.

decisions.choice: to this day: until the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As in verse 13 and at 8:8, "to this day" means the time when the book was written.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" is kept at every level because slavery itself is the point: verse 22 sets these peoples against the Israelites, whom Solomon did not make slaves.

decisions.choice: destroy completely
decisions.reason: Readable uses the book-wide wording for this verb.

records.source: וּמִבְּנֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹֽא־נָתַ֥ן שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה עָ֑בֶד כִּי־הֵ֞ם אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וַעֲבָדָיו֙ וְשָׂרָ֣יו וְשָׁלִשָׁ֔יו וְשָׂרֵ֥י רִכְבּ֖וֹ וּפָרָשָֽׁיו׃ס
records.gloss: But of [the] sons of Israel not made Solomon a slave, for they [were] the men of the war and his servants and his commanders and his officers and [the] commanders of his chariotry and his horsemen.
pieces: But Solomon did not make slaves of any of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They were his soldiers, his officials, his commanders, his officers, and the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.

L.22: But of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel Solomon did not make a slave; for they [were] the men of war, and his servants and his commanders and his officers and the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.

R.22: But Solomon did not make any of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} his slaves. Instead, they served as his soldiers, his officials and his commanders. They were his officers, and they commanded his chariots and his horsemen.

decisions.choice: Solomon did not make a slave of Israelites: they were not put into permanent servitude
decisions.reason: Earlier, Solomon raised forced labor "from all Israel", thirty thousand men working in shifts (5:27-28), and the complaints about his heavy yoke led to the split of the kingdom (12:4). The two statements fit if the Israelites did spells of service while the remaining Canaanite peoples were held as permanent slaves.

decisions.choice: his servants and his commanders: the king's officials and military leaders
decisions.reason: "His servants" are the men in the king's service at court; "commanders" are leaders in the army.

decisions.choice: officers: a rank in the army
decisions.reason: The word comes from "three" and may first have meant the third man in a chariot. It came to name a high-ranking officer (2 Kings 9:25; 10:25).

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" is kept at every level, as in verse 21, because the verse is about who was made a slave.

decisions.choice: soldiers; officials
decisions.reason: "Men of war" is plain "soldiers" at Balanced and Readable, and the king's "servants" are his officials.

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה׀שָׂרֵ֣י הַנִּצָּבִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר עַל־הַמְּלָאכָה֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וַחֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת הָרֹדִ֣ים בָּעָ֔ם הָעֹשִׂ֖ים בַּמְּלָאכָֽה׃
records.gloss: These [were] [the] chiefs of the officers who [were] over the work for Solomon, fifty and five hundreds, who ruled over the people who were doing the work.
pieces: These were the chief officers in charge of Solomon's work: 550 of them, who directed the people doing the work.

L.23: These [were] the chiefs of the officers who [were] over the work for Solomon: 550, who ruled over the people doing the work.

R.23: There were 550 chief officers in charge of Solomon's building work. They directed the people who did the work.

decisions.choice: 550 chief officers
decisions.reason: 5:30 counts 3,300 officials over the workers, and 2 Chronicles 8:10 counts 250 chief officers, with 3,600 overseers in 2 Chronicles 2:17. The numbers likely count different ranks; both books give the same total, 3,850 (3,300 and 550; 3,600 and 250).

decisions.choice: chiefs of the officers: the men set over the work gangs
decisions.reason: The second word means someone stationed or appointed; the same word names Solomon's district officers (4:5, 7). Here they supervise the building work.

decisions.choice: ruled over: directed, kept in order
decisions.reason: The verb is used of masters over workers and need not mean harshness, though it can (Leviticus 25:43).

decisions.choice: directed
decisions.reason: "Directed" gives the supervising sense without the overtones of "ruled".

records.source: אַ֣ךְ בַּת־פַּרְעֹ֗ה עָֽלְתָה֙ מֵעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔ד אֶל־בֵּיתָ֖הּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּֽנָה־לָ֑הּ אָ֖ז בָּנָ֥ה אֶת־הַמִּלּֽוֹא׃
records.gloss: Only [the] daughter of Pharaoh went up from [the] city of David to her house which he had built for her; then he built the Millo.
pieces: Once Pharaoh's daughter had moved up from the city of David to the house Solomon had built for her, he built the Millo.

L.24: Only [when] the daughter of Pharaoh had gone up from the city of David to her house that he had built for her, then he built the Millo.

R.24: Pharaoh's daughter moved from the city of David to the palace Solomon had built for her. After that, Solomon built the Millo.

decisions.choice: only when ... then: the Millo was built after Pharaoh's daughter moved
decisions.reason: The opening word usually means "only" or "surely"; with "then" it sets the order of events: the Millo was built after she had moved. Why the move came first is not said.

decisions.choice: her house that he had built for her: the palace of 7:8
decisions.reason: Solomon had brought Pharaoh's daughter to the city of David until his building was finished (3:1), and he built her a house like his own hall (7:8).

decisions.choice: went up from the city of David: up to the higher ground north of the old city
decisions.reason: The city of David lay on the lower southern ridge; the palace and temple stood higher up to the north.

decisions.choice: Solomon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Solomon for "he", and Readable calls the house a palace.

records.source: וְהֶעֱלָ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֡ה שָׁלֹשׁ֩ פְּעָמִ֨ים בַּשָּׁנָ֜ה עֹל֣וֹת וּשְׁלָמִ֗ים עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֣ה לַיהוָ֔ה וְהַקְטֵ֣יר אִתּ֔וֹאֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְשִׁלַּ֖ם אֶת־הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And offered up Solomon three times in the year burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar which he had built for Yahweh, and burning with it which [was] before Yahweh; and he completed the house.
pieces: Three times a year Solomon would present burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he himself had built for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and with them he burned incense before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And so he finished the house.

L.25: And Solomon would offer up, three times in the year, burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he had built for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, burning [incense] with it, [the altar] that [was] before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and he completed the house.

R.25: Every year, three times, Solomon presented burnt offerings and peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the altar he had built. He also burned incense to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So Solomon finished the temple.

decisions.choice: three times in the year: the three great feasts
decisions.reason: The law required every man to appear before the LORD three times a year, at the feasts of Unleavened Bread, Weeks and Booths (Exodus 23:14-17; Deuteronomy 16:16).

decisions.choice: would offer: a regular practice
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe something done again and again, year after year, not a single event.

decisions.choice: burning with it, that was before the LORD: probably incense on the altar before the LORD
alternatives: burning the offerings on it before the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is compressed: "and burning with it that before the LORD". It may mean that Solomon also burned incense on the gold altar that stood before the LORD inside the house (6:20-22; 7:48), or that he burned the offerings on the altar already named.

decisions.choice: he completed the house: the work on the temple was brought to its end
alternatives: he kept up the house's worship
decisions.reason: The verb means to make complete or whole. It may round off the account of the building, or mean that Solomon kept the temple's worship complete by these offerings.

decisions.choice: peace offerings; incense supplied
decisions.reason: "Peace offerings" follows the book-wide wording. "Incense" is supplied for the verb "burning", bracketed at Literal.

records.source: וָאֳנִ֡י עָשָׂה֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה בְּעֶצְיֽוֹן־גֶּ֨בֶר אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֶת־אֵל֛וֹת עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת יַם־ס֖וּף בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And a fleet of ships made the king Solomon at Ezion Geber which [is] near Eloth on [the] shore of [the] Sea of Reeds in [the] land of Edom.
pieces: King Solomon also built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, near Eloth in the land of Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.

L.26: And King Solomon made a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which [is] beside Eloth on the shore of the Sea of Reeds, in the land of Edom.

R.26: King Solomon also built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber. This town is near Eloth, on the Red Sea coast in the land of Edom.

decisions.choice: Ezion-geber and Eloth: ports at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba
decisions.reason: Both lay at the northern tip of the eastern arm of the Red Sea, on the route Israel took in the wilderness (Numbers 33:35; Deuteronomy 2:8, where Eloth is spelled Elath). From there ships could sail south to Arabia and Africa.

decisions.choice: Sea of Reeds: the Red Sea, here its Gulf of Aqaba
decisions.reason: The name means "sea of reeds". It is used of the sea Israel crossed (Exodus 15:4) and of the gulf east of Sinai (Numbers 21:4).

decisions.choice: in the land of Edom: in territory under Solomon's control
decisions.reason: David had put garrisons in Edom (2 Samuel 8:14), so this coast was in Israel's hands.

decisions.choice: fleet of ships: a group of ships
decisions.reason: The noun names ships as a group.

decisions.choice: Red Sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name, as in Exodus; Literal keeps "Sea of Reeds".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח חִירָ֤ם בָּֽאֳנִי֙ אֶת־עֲבָדָ֔יו אַנְשֵׁ֣י אֳנִיּ֔וֹת יֹדְעֵ֖י הַיָּ֑ם עִ֖ם עַבְדֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And sent Hiram in the fleet his servants, men of ships knowing the sea, with [the] servants of Solomon.
pieces: Hiram sent his own servants with the fleet, sailors who knew the sea, to serve alongside Solomon's servants.

L.27: And Hiram sent in the fleet his servants, men of ships who knew the sea, with the servants of Solomon.

R.27: Hiram sent some of his men, experienced sailors who knew the sea, to go with Solomon's men.

decisions.choice: men of ships who knew the sea: experienced sailors from Tyre
decisions.reason: The Phoenicians of Tyre were the great seafarers of the age (Ezekiel 27), while Israel had little experience of the sea. Hiram's skilled crews made the voyages possible.

decisions.choice: servants: men in the king's service
decisions.reason: Here the word means men under each king's command, sailors and crew, not court officials.

decisions.choice: men
decisions.reason: Readable says "men" for those in each king's service, since they were sailors, not officials. Balanced adds "to serve" to make the partnership clear.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אוֹפִ֔ירָה וַיִּקְח֤וּ מִשָּׁם֙ זָהָ֔ב אַרְבַּע־מֵא֥וֹת וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים כִּכָּ֑ר וַיָּבִ֖אוּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And they went to Ophir and took from there gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought [it] to the king Solomon.
pieces: They went to Ophir and brought back from there {{units:about 31,500 pounds|420 talents}} of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon.

L.28: And they went to Ophir and took from there gold, 420 talents, and brought [it] to King Solomon.

R.28: They sailed to Ophir and brought back {{units:about 31,500 pounds|420 talents}} of gold for King Solomon.

decisions.choice: Ophir: a distant land famous for its gold
decisions.reason: Its location is not known; southern Arabia, the coast of East Africa and India have all been suggested. "Gold of Ophir" was a byword for the finest gold (Isaiah 13:12; Psalm 45:10; Job 28:16).

decisions.choice: 420 talents: 2 Chronicles 8:18 has 450
decisions.reason: The parallel account gives a slightly different figure. 420 talents is about 31,500 pounds, some 16 tons.

decisions.choice: about 31,500 pounds (with 420 talents as the setting)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern weight, with the talent as the alternative, as in verse 14.

decisions.choice: sailed
decisions.reason: Readable says "sailed", since they went by ship (verse 27).
